_comment: Shared test vectors for claim-code normalisation, consumed by BOTH
normalizeCode is the canonicalisation contract with the database: hashCode
runs on its output, so if the TypeScript and Go implementations disagree by
even one byte, a code minted on one side cannot be claimed from the other.
The failure is silent — it surfaces as a 404 that is deliberately
indistinguishable from a wrong guess. Hence one fixture, two readers.

valid.why: mnemonic dictated and retyped with spaces
surrounding whitespace from a sloppy paste
a word containing a hyphen survives, which is why the separator is a dot
legacy base32 with the EM- prefix
legacy: I misread for 1 is recovered — folding that would destroy a mnemonic
legacy: O misread for 0 is recovered

invalid.why: shorter than the minimum even after space folding
shell metacharacters are refused; the code goes into a paste-ready command
uppercase-only junk that is not 16 chars of base32
